instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Hand It Over
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to give up control of a task, object, or decision you believe is being mishandled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. Let me fix that cupboard hinge. The door's lower than when you started.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm just finding the right screw.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. You've tried four. Give me the screwdriver while you find it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you'll tell everyone you fixed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can announce the repair. I'll stand behind you with the screwdriver, keeping the door attached.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the seating-plan pencil. I taught you to host, and you've put the exes beside each other.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're civil now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you noticed the improvement. I haven't yet taught you the difference between civil and trapped. Let me separate their places.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I spent hours getting the table numbers even.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you finally got the arithmetic right. I'll keep every total; you read me the numbers while I move the names.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Put It Back Quietly
cards.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your umbrella's back in its stand. Remember how I taught you to check your things before work? Handle's clean.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is the canopy wet? It hasn't rained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've moved beyond the handle. I gave it a rinse; let me dry it properly for you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's pondweed in the spokes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Very thorough, at last. Have breakfast while I finish cleaning it. You can inspect the spokes again when it's back where it belongs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your plate's back in the cupboard. I taught you to set a welcoming table; those flowers will help on Sunday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Our plates were plain. Where did that one come from?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, your eye for a pattern is improving. I'll use the flowered one and cover it with potatoes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: No. I want six matching plates, not you hiding one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're finally thinking about the whole table. I'll get five more flowered ones. Leave the plain ones in the cupboard; we'll use my new arrangement on Sunday.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Talk Around the Mess
cards.instruction: Keep attention on minor details so no one addresses the larger responsibility you avoided.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mum's coming for lunch. I taught you to check the little things: does this spoon look clean enough?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's fine. You were supposed to clean the whole kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you remember the brief. Now look at the forks; she notices water spots.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've asked her to bring gloves and help you with the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've finally learned to welcome help. Find a towel for her hands, then. Not the faded one—I taught you better than that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to organize a move before lifting a thing. Blue or green labels for these boxes?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You were meant to pack them. They're empty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you checked the contents. Now learn to prevent confusion: which color says bedroom?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The van's outside. The driver wants something to load.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent, a fresh pair of eyes. Ask him which label he'd recognize upstairs. Show him both; don't rush the comparison like you used to.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Spare Them the Hassle
cards.instruction: Hide a practical problem because you believe handling it alone is kinder than involving anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've been on the ward all night. I taught you to rest after caring for everyone else; sit down and I'll bring lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is there a bucket by my chair?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you still notice things when you're tired. Just a drip. Take the sofa; your tray's ready.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll eat upstairs and go straight to bed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Rest first, as I taught you. I'll bring the duvet down and finish airing your room. You don't need another job after that shift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An afternoon off means off. I taught you that. Stay with your book; I'll have your bike ready tomorrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The repair shop wants me to collect a wheel. Where's the rest?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you read the whole message this time. Leave the collection to me; the ticket still has your number.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Another shop just rang about the frame. Do you need me to come?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're finally offering before being asked. No, keep reading. I've made one little route for the parts; you can practise letting someone look after you.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Who Changed It?
cards.instruction: Ask innocent questions until someone admits altering the plan, schedule, arrangement, or shared space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to keep this calendar clear. The picnic's moved from Saturday to Friday; whose blue pen is that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine, but everyone borrows it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're considering every possibility. Which of us still uses the little hearts from our old handwriting lessons?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right, I changed it. Friday suits me better.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you can use 'I' after all. Who's going to tell the Saturday guests?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to leave space around furniture. Was this sofa always in front of the cupboard?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's room for yoga now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you remembered one part. Did making that space involve somebody moving the sofa?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes, I moved it. I put your mugs somewhere easier to reach.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're finally thinking ahead. Would that be the sock drawer, or is there another storage method I haven't taught you yet?
